title: Outlaws of Thunder Junction: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Weary travelers trade stories of the Eversaloon, an extraplanar respite that appears at the moment it is most needed.
"I always wanted to ride a slow cannonball with legs!" —Kellan
No one could prove the ox did it, but no one tried to harness it again either.
When Kellan questioned her, Eriette reminded him that she'd been asked only to put the guard to sleep—the request said nothing about waking up.
As the vault collapsed around them, Kellan made sure Akul couldn't follow them out.
After it passed by, the rancher swore she saw hope shining in the pigs' eyes.
"We must forge for ourselves the gifts that nature neglected to give us."
Kellan had no plan. He simply poured his focus into the train and willed it to stop.
"Count yourself lucky I came upon you. This is not a world of second chances."
Freestriders took to patrolling near the Omenpaths, protecting new arrivals from the robbers and charlatans prowling for easy marks.
"What are you gonna do, walk a hundred miles for a second opinion?"
The Freestriders believe in liberation, in all its many forms.
"Release the cows!"
It catches those who are not ready to fall.
"Just because you can saddle a critter, doesn't mean it'll let you ride." —Annie Flash
"If you don't want to tell me where the stash is, you'd best start getting comfy in there. You just let me know when you've changed your mind."
The Sterling Company can always rely on him to bring the thunder.
The frontier was an anvil on which many an unlikely hero would be forged.
"The Sterling Company says they protect us, but where are they when the Hellspurs burn half the town? Counting their vaults!"
Many a would-be captor has gotten close enough to count its feathers, only to be left behind with nothing but regret and a dangling rope.
They cluster near shallow river crossings, blending into the rocks, waiting for unsuspecting travelers to step within range of their claws.
It's amazing how many sticky situations you can get out of simply by being ten times faster than anyone expects.
"Heard you've been horning in on my turf. How about I introduce you to some surf?"
No one knew if the waterfall was a natural wonder the djinn guarded or if he'd conjured it to hide something even greater.
The best alibi is being in multiple places at the same time.
Nathan Steuer, World Champion XXVIII
"We should have taken the blasted ferry!" —Hope Hagan, prospector
"You're not mad I pulled a little prank. You're just mad you fell for it." —Oko, to Annie Flash
As mating season approaches, drakes dive through scalding geysers, revealing the brightly colored scales hidden beneath layers of dust.
It can see in both darkness and daylight, but it hunts best when thunder growls in the sky.
Satoru insisted he was just about to free himself.
She poses a riddle to each mark, allowing them a chance to keep their goods. Thus far, none have succeeded.
Rundo's craving for revenge was replaced by a craving for vegetables.
The hard part wasn't sneaking aboard. It was safely exiting with Slickshot flair.
"Murder someone and you'll have a gaggle of folks lining up for revenge. Humiliate them, and they won't dare bother you again."
To his enemies' chagrin, Winston was every bit as meddlesome dead as he had been alive.
"Now you see me, now you—"
Nolan refused to give up the vault's location. The strange figure simply smiled and reached into his mind.
Even when he missed the wrists, a pair of thundercuffs to the head got the job done.
"Sure it's risky, but that's what makes it fun! That and the money. And the bankers' faces."
It once escaped a cook's pot. Now it fears neither heat nor human.
Dewey had been briefed on every aspect of the plan... except the bit where he was left holding the bag.
"All that fancy footwork, and you can't even dodge one silly little rope? Cryin' shame, that is."
She'd planned for every eventuality, with the obvious exception of failure.
"First rule of crossing Blacksnag Bog: if you can't see the bottom, don't." —Chance Mulligan, wilderness guide
"The tighter I bind them, the looser their tongues become."
It's never too late to start an afterlife of crime.
The enforcer only got halfway through the arrest warrant before it—and he—went up in smoke.
Every moving carriage is an accident waiting to happen, and the Hellspurs hate waiting.
He was glad when the mirages appeared. At least he wouldn't die alone.
With no mammals around, some vampires tried to feed on cactusfolk, with horrible results for everyone involved.
"Oh, he's done bothering us. Trust me." —Dwayne, Hellspur guard
Akul didn't know what lay inside Tarnation's great vault, but the mystery fueled his obsession.
"Now rip your partner from the grave, and form an undead killing wave!"
"Y'all should've known better than to buy me a coffin!"
"Don't bother getting up. I'll see myself in."
"If they want to get to Prosperity so badly, they can walk there."
Not everyone can be a pickpocket.
"Looking for a little liquid courage? I also stock liquid murder, if that's what you're after."
A raven sighted at midnight often means there's unkindness on the way.
"Sneaking behind people? Pedestrian."
"Now, where is that deputy?" —Jana, Hellspur thunderslinger
"Why you yellow-bellied, loot-stealing, good-for-nothing, bottom-feeding, dog-faced, lily-livered..."
It was going to be the greatest heist of his unlife.
The old miners' trail across Blacksnag Bog is littered with lost fortunes and the bones of those who searched for them.
"Looks like you've got a train to catch." —Laughing Jasper Flint
"Kind of them to put all their valuables in the same place."
Slickshots are always eager to demonstrate their skills to whomever questions them.
"Can I interest you in some herbs from Naktamun? Fresh from the Omenpath! Or a set of Fioran cookware? Finest in the Multiverse!"
"BOMBS AND TRAINS AND SABOTAGE!" —Breeches
For years afterward, lucky explorers who found the cave could chip gold fragments off the rocky walls.
The last fool who called him "cowboy" earned a free ride to the bottom of Blacksnag Bog.
The fires weren't even out before the backstabbing began.
"The 3:10 to Omenport will be delayed." —Prosperity Station announcement
"I didn't miss. Blasted thing snatched my bolt out of the air and ate it!" —Lilah, Slickshot boss
The only witness to their rampage was the stoic visage of the moon.
They grew together, awoke together, and took up arms together. If they were going to fall, they'd do that together too.
The opening of the Omenpaths awoke the wild magic of Thunder Junction. Settlers dubbed it "thunder" and put it to use in everything from farming tools to deadly weapons.
"First to the fray, first to the pay!"
"Chasing the roadrunner" —Omenport slang for wasting energy on impossible pursuits
"Don't you know it's rude not to share?"
"My citizens throw good money at them, and for what? Cheap tricks and collateral damage. Damnable Slickshot charlatans." —Baron Bertram Graywater
The herd followed him through an Omenpath and found their curiosity rewarded with an untamed world rich with unsuspecting prey.
Most outlaws prefer to strike when there are no witnesses. Slickshots prefer as many as possible.
"Your horse deserves a braver rider!"
"You said one weapon in the duel. Ain't my fault you forgot to specify size."
"Cowerin' behind your buddy ain't gonna help, ya yellow-bellied lowlife." —Tyron, Slickshot duelist
"Little tip, newcomer. Give your boots a shake in the morning before you put them on." —Annie Flash, to Kellan
The vault cracked open, and the unlikely alliance met the likeliest of ends, as greed, rage, and self-interest won out over any shred of loyalty.
As she defends them in their youth, they shall someday defend her in her old age.
"Wake up, little ones. There's a new day ahead."
The runaway train tore through the manicured streets of Prosperity, its new conductors reveling in the sheer destruction.
"Don't believe anyone who tells you to bite it. If it's the real thing, you'll know."
Visitors to the town of Hardbristle found the locals to be quite prickly.
"Never get too cocky. Remember you stay upright only by your mount's good graces."
Pioneers with a distaste for crowds and cities are welcomed by the Outcasters, who celebrate solitude and find endless wonder in the natural world.
In the shade of his sword, the desert blooms.
The Atiin delight in delving into the unique wonders of each world they visit.
It's not hard to know the right song for the occasion when most occasions are saloon brawls.
Most travelers panic when they stumble upon the skin of a giant rattlewurm. Landry saw it as a gift.
"A little kindness would've carried you a lot farther than those spurs." —Miriam, herd whisperer
When weeds tumble against the wind, *run*.
"A varmint's diet consists of anything it can fit into its mouth and a surprising number of things it can't." —Doc Aurlock
One last job, then she could retire in peace.
The cactusfolk were a young culture, but they already knew the pains of death and joys of birth.
"Of course the law's on my side. I wrote it."
"Learning stops only when you close your mind off to wonder."
"Your dreams and mine will soon align."
The terms were simple: half in advance, half when the entire town belonged to their employer.
"No questions. No refunds."
The nomadic Atiin rarely settle anywhere for more than a few seasons, but Jem never lets that stop her from seeing every last corner.
"So, are we doing this the easy way or the fun way?"
"I found out who I was. Now it's time to discover who I am."
Concerned for his apprentice's welfare, Ludevic sent his greatest creation to make sure Geralf got into the right kind of trouble.
"Aim alone won't win you a duel if you can't keep your nerve." —Annie Flash
"It's funny how rarely folks here think to look up."
"Anything willing to bear your weight and save your feet a trip across the hot sands deserves respect. Show some."
"You're living on borrowed time."
There's only one law that truly matters to the Sterling Company: never stand in the way of profit.
"This backwater doesn't have a single wall, ward, or guard that could keep me out."
"Shooting first don't mean much if you ain't got proper follow-through."
"You'd best keep yourself out of my sights."
It wasn't quite home, but the fire still burned bright and the bombs still went boom.
Letting Oko believe he held all the cards provided the perfect cover for her own scheme to unfold.
"Unfinished business goes both ways, pal."
The cruel irony of explosives is they're most interesting exactly when you should be running away as fast as you can.
These boots were made for far more than walking.
"I think the blasted thing's actually attracting *more* birds, but all the same, the garden's never looked better." —Jay Marigold, homesteader
The miners thought it would be genius to increase their productivity with explosives. The land thought otherwise.
It couldn't comprehend the spirit of the law, so the Sterling Company settled for the letter.
"Beware of Cog" —Prosperity courthouse sign
"Dying is common on Thunder Junction. Resting in peace is a much rarer commodity." —Baron Bertram Graywater
"The wind passing through the grooves makes a strange sort of music here." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
"The cacti have it right. Always carry water." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
The newly constructed relays harness the desert sun, bringing power to settlers across the plane.
"The sunsets in Spinegully sure make the soul question why we bother with cities." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
"The water looks like liquid gold. Wonder how many died trying to bottle it." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
"Lost a boot in the muck. Get the feeling I'm lucky I got to keep the leg." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
"Should have known that shine on the horizon wasn't water." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
"Tense day of travel. Couldn't shake the feeling those peaks were about to topple." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
"Barely dodged a stampede yesterday. Took all night for the dust to settle." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
"Finally, a stroke of luck! Had to taste the water myself to believe it wasn't a mirage." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
"Out there, death and salvation may lie on either side of the same ridge of sand." —Ertha Jo, frontier mentor
"Ever been caught out in a storm like that? Think of it like drowning, but all the water is knives." —Annie Flash
"Groundwater's tainted here. Best push on before our canteens run out." —Pioneer journal of Big Ralph
They both knew only one of them would walk away.
Lucky travelers reported a mighty winged creature among the geysers. Unlucky ones didn't make it back.
Akul saw his Hellspur followers as little more than ammunition to be expended.
The key is to slay it before it sprouts so many heads that your fear outpaces your greed.
Crackling with rage and stolen thunder, he drives the Hellspurs to ever-greater heights of violence.
"I find a world where the herds finally listen to me, but now the *plants* have an attitude?"
"The Conclave was soft. The Clans were trapped beasts. Here in this untamed wilderness, nature can truly roam free."
"You should have folded when you had the chance."
"I've seen a fair few worlds in my travels, and there's always some lowlife looking to prey on the innocent. That's where I come in."
